transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Maya. Could I get your account number and PIN to pull up your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Maya, sure, account is 245-810-963, PIN 7724. This is Ben Torres.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks Ben, that matches, you're verified. What can I help with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our VoIP desk phone at the front desk, extension 102, has been crackling and sometimes dropping calls entirely, started about three days ago. It's the one my receptionist uses to take client calls, so it's a pretty visible problem for us.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, so extension 102 at the front desk has had crackling audio and occasional full drops for about three days now, and it's client-facing so it's been noticeable. That's frustrating when it's the phone people actually hear you on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly, we've had two clients mention it sounded like we were breaking up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the kind of thing that sticks with a client, understandably. How long have you had that phone system set up with us, roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: About eight months now, it's been solid until this week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good to know, so this is a new problem, not something that's always been there.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We do have a backup line, but it's honestly not set up for the call volume we get some days.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That makes sense, so with most of the volume running through this one line, any hiccup on it is going to be felt right away by the whole front desk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly, that's kind of the frustrating part.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood, let's get this sorted then. I'm going to have you reboot that phone first, that usually clears up intermittent audio issues like this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how long should I expect it to be offline for?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It shouldn't take too long.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, unplugging it now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's booted back up, showing registered again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, can you make a quick test call and see how the audio sounds?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, calling my cell now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hmm, still a bit of crackling actually, not as bad but still there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that tells us it's probably not just a phone-side glitch. Let's check the network side. Is that phone on WiFi or plugged in directly with an ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on ethernet, plugged straight into our switch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, that rules out WiFi interference. How many other devices are on that same switch, roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Maybe six or seven, a couple of computers, another phone, a printer, and our card reader.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, and has anything changed recently on the network, new equipment added, anything like that, around when this started three days ago?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually yes, we added a second WiFi access point around then for better coverage in the back office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a useful data point, when exactly was that installed relative to when the crackling started?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I think it was the day before, so pretty close together timing-wise.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a strong lead then. Is that access point plugged into the same switch as the phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, same switch as everything else.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, let's check something called QoS, or quality of service, on the router, it prioritizes voice traffic so calls don't get crowded out by other network activity. Can you check if that's enabled?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... I don't see anything obviously labeled QoS in the settings I have access to.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's alright, I can check it from our side since it's our equipment. Give me a moment to pull that up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see QoS is currently off on your router. Enabling it and prioritizing the VoIP traffic specifically should stop other devices, especially that new access point, from crowding out your call audio.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that makes sense actually, right around when we added the new access point.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, extra devices competing for bandwidth is a really common cause of exactly this kind of crackling. Let me enable QoS now and set voice traffic as the priority.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Done, that's applied. Let's test again, can you make another call?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, calling now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds completely clear now, no crackling at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's great to hear. So the fix was two parts really, the phone reboot cleared any lingering session issue, and enabling QoS with voice prioritized should prevent the new access point or anything else on that switch from crowding out call audio going forward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes a lot of sense, appreciate you actually tracking down why instead of just having me reboot things blindly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is QoS something I could have turned on myself if I'd known to look for it, or is that only accessible on your end?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's actually on the router's admin page, so you could access it, but the specific voice-priority configuration we just did is a bit more particular, easy to get wrong if you're not familiar with it, so I'd recommend calling in for that part specifically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough, good to know it's there if I ever want to peek at it though.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For sure, happy to walk you through the settings page anytime if you're curious.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, that's what I'm here for. Now, what extension did you say was affected again, just so I log it properly on the ticket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's extension 102, the front desk one, same as I mentioned at the start of the call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, sorry, I've got that noted, extension 102.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No worries. Should I keep an eye on it for a while just to be sure, or is this pretty much confirmed fixed now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd keep half an eye on it for the rest of today just to be safe, but the QoS change directly addresses the cause we found, so I'd expect it to hold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sounds good, I'll check in with my receptionist later and see how it's been.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. If it does act up again, mention the QoS change was already made today so whoever you reach doesn't have to start from scratch diagnosing it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do, that's a good tip. Is there anything else I should watch for with the new access point, or was this really just the one setting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: This was really just the one setting for this particular symptom. If you add more devices to that switch in the future, it's worth checking QoS priorities again, but for now this should hold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it, that's good to know for planning ahead.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Would the QoS change affect anything else on that switch, like the computers or the card reader?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good question, it shouldn't slow those down in any noticeable way, we only bumped voice traffic ahead in priority, everything else still gets normal bandwidth, it just won't get to jump the line ahead of a call anymore.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that's good, wouldn't want to fix one thing and slow something else down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Makes sense to ask. While I have you, want me to check if your router's firmware is up to date? That can sometimes contribute to network hiccups too, and it's a quick check from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Give me about twenty seconds to pull that up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good news, it's already on the current version, so that's not a factor here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, one less thing to worry about.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the other phone on that switch ever have this issue, or has it really just been the front desk one?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: From what you've described it sounds like just the front desk extension so far, but if the other one starts acting up too, the same QoS fix should already be covering it since it's applied at the router level, not per phone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh good, so we wouldn't have to redo this if it shows up on the other line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, this one change covers voice traffic for the whole office, not just extension 102.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's reassuring, that was actually going to be my next question.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more thing, is there a way to get an alert if call quality drops again, or would we only find out from a client mentioning it like this time?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unfortunately nothing automatic on our end for that specifically, you'd notice it the way you did this time, through a call sounding off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, fair enough, at least we know what to check now if it happens again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, and the account notes will have today's fix documented, so it'll be quick to reference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. I think that covers it for today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Anything else I can help with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything, thank you Maya.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Ben. We do value your feedback, so please stay on the line after this call for a short survey. Thank you for choosing S-Net, have a great rest of your day.
